- A same-build comparison on seeds 13–32 resolves about 0.1 pp.

- Stem freeze saves about 0.0087 s per step at 32 px.

- E054: skipping the stem backward on every second 28 px step (~35 steps) saved 0.21 s, about 0.006 s per skipped step. That fits the model. My time misses (E046, E052) were both savings I underestimated. Removal-type changes save a bit more than the MAC model says because overhead goes with them, so I keep a −2% bias on those.

**Exchange rates (s saved per pp lost):**
- Epoch dial: about 1–2.5.
- Stem freeze at 75%: about 2.
- Group-2 freeze at 90%: close to free.
- Group-2 freeze at 85%: no better than the dial (discarded).
- Stem freeze at 60%: a cliff (about 0.65).
- Intermittent stem at 28 px (E054): −0.2 to −0.35 pp for 0.21 s, so about 0.7–1, worse than the dial.
- Width: about 0.7. Stride instead of pool: about 0.45.

**What I think the stem needs.** It must keep adapting continuously through the 28 px phase and into 32 px. E037, E042 and E054 all say that reducing the stem's update signal before about 75% costs more than the dial. So moving the freeze to 71% probably costs on a linear-to-convex dose curve, about −0.1 pp for about −0.08 s. That is roughly the dial's rate, not a free lunch.

**Funders.** Every booster tested has read ≤0. My prior for a new one is −0.05 ± 0.2 pp. Accuracy is bought with steps.

**Mechanisms.**
1. Lookahead is worth about 1 pp and is near its optimum.
2. The late 28/32 px phases carry accuracy, and so does a stem that keeps training until about 75%.
3. Early accuracy depends on step count and the LR schedule, not on pixels.
4. The free part of backward truncation is used up. Further truncation costs about the dial's rate or worse.
5. Muon renormalizes the filters, so filter wd has no effect.
6. Removing inductive priors (pool, GELU) costs more than the dial.

**Strategy.**
- What remains are systems levers at identical math (the Cin=24 padding, launch overhead), or a deliberate step increase to restore about 0.2 pp of population margin before the judge.
- Conditional stacking ideas whose components failed should be dropped.

**Unsure.**
- Whether ReLU's fused backward saves ≥3%. I lean toward 1.5–2.5%, because the BN-input read dominates the bytes.

W3 (cost lens), after E054.

**Tip (E049, 3df6233).** E036 plus a group-2 freeze (LR annealed from 75%, frozen for the last 10%) plus 0.25 extra epoch: 237 steps at batch 2000.
- Resolution: 20/24/28/32 px at 30/10/30/30%. Whitening detached from 20%, stem frozen from 75%.
- Two builds read 0.7535 / 5.198 s and 0.7552 / 5.206 s. I put the population mean at about 0.7535–0.754, which leaves almost no margin for the PCIe judge.

**Noise.**
- Across rebuilds of identical math, the 3-seed mean moves about ±0.25 pp. Per-seed std is about 0.3 pp.
- Time reproduces to about 1%.
- A same-build comparison on seeds 13–32 resolves about 0.1 pp.
- Seeds 0–2 can't detect effects under 0.2 pp. E052 and E053 read above 0.755 there and were still discarded on held-out seeds.

**Time model.** Time ≈ 0.25 s + Σ (steps × per-step cost).
- Per-step cost: 32 px 0.032 s, 28 px 0.026 s, 24 px 0.021 s, 20 px 0.016 s.
- Stem freeze saves about 0.0087 s per step at 32 px.
- The group-2 freeze saves a further ~0.010 s per step.
- E054: skipping the stem backward on every second 28 px step (~35 steps) saved 0.21 s, about 0.006 s per skipped step. That fits the model. My time misses (E046, E052) were both savings I underestimated. Removal-type changes save a bit more than the MAC model says because overhead goes with them, so I keep a −2% bias on those.

**Exchange rates (s saved per pp lost):**
- Epoch dial: about 1–2.5.
- Stem freeze at 75%: about 2.
- Group-2 freeze at 90%: close to free.
- Group-2 freeze at 85%: no better than the dial (discarded).
- Stem freeze at 60%: a cliff (about 0.65).
- Intermittent stem at 28 px (E054): −0.2 to −0.35 pp for 0.21 s, so about 0.7–1, worse than the dial.
- Width: about 0.7. Stride instead of pool: about 0.45.

**What I think the stem needs.** It must keep adapting continuously through the 28 px phase and into 32 px. E037, E042 and E054 all say that reducing the stem's update signal before about 75% costs more than the dial. So moving the freeze to 71% probably costs on a linear-to-convex dose curve, about −0.1 pp for about −0.08 s. That is roughly the dial's rate, not a free lunch.

**Funders.** Every booster tested has read ≤0. My prior for a new one is −0.05 ± 0.2 pp. Accuracy is bought with steps.

**Mechanisms.**
1. Lookahead is worth about 1 pp and is near its optimum.
2. The late 28/32 px phases carry accuracy, and so does a stem that keeps training until about 75%.
3. Early accuracy depends on step count and the LR schedule, not on pixels.
4. The free part of backward truncation is used up. Further truncation costs about the dial's rate or worse.
5. Muon renormalizes the filters, so filter wd has no effect.
6. Removing inductive priors (pool, GELU) costs more than the dial.

**Strategy.**
- What remains are systems levers at identical math (the Cin=24 padding, launch overhead), or a deliberate step increase to restore about 0.2 pp of population margin before the judge.
- Conditional stacking ideas whose components failed should be dropped.

**Unsure.**
- Whether ReLU's fused backward saves ≥3%. I lean toward 1.5–2.5%, because the BN-input read dominates the bytes.
- Whether H4.4 is winner's curse or seed-set difficulty.

forecasts.reason: About 9 more frozen 32 px steps at ~0.0087 s each saves about 0.08 s (~1.5%). E037, E042 and E054 suggest about −0.1 pp, which lands at the 0.1 pp threshold; same-build power is too weak to settle it.
The fused BN+GELU backward is dominated by reading the BN input and the grad, so ReLU saves about 1.5–2.5%, likely below the 3% gate. If it does run, ReLU likely costs about 0.15–0.25 pp.
Both component cuts failed (I082/E053 and E054 were discarded), so by its own rule this collapses to tip plus 0.25 epoch: slower than E049 with about +0.08 pp. It can't meet the ≥1.5% time cut.

cruxes: Is there an identical-math systems lever (zero-padding Cin=24 to 32, fewer launches or less optimizer/Lookahead overhead) worth ≥2%? It is the only class of change that avoids the dial's ~1.5 s/pp exchange rate.
Does the stem-freeze dose curve from 75% down to 71% cost little or about −0.1 pp? That decides whether any truncation room is left.
What is the tip's true population mean on unselected seeds (≥0.754 or ≈0.7535)? It decides whether the next move must spend time on a margin top-up rather than on cuts.
